$comment: Every rendered verdict on this page carries a data-verdict marker, and every marker listed here has been forced false and watched go red. A mutation counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the same run, the failure was that marker's OWN assertion, and the run served the mutated bundle (CI=1, port 4684, no reused server). e2e/verdicts.spec.ts fails on any rendered marker missing from this file.

dleq.renders: #dleq — whether the client accepted the issuer's DLEQ proof under the key it was told to trust

mutations.kills: e2e/claims.spec.ts:57 expect(getByText('DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED')).toBeVisible()
mutations.observed: 1 failed / 12 passed: the unpublished-key mode stopped aborting and rendered 'DLEQ PROOF · ACCEPTED AN UNPUBLISHED KEY'

redemption.renders: #redeem-verdict — whether the origin accepted or refused the token presented to it

mutations.mutation: delete `this.spent.add(nonceId)` so a redeemed nonce is never recorded
mutations.observed: 2 failed / 11 passed: the replay was accepted, so the verdict read 'REDEMPTION · VERIFIED' and the integrity oracle painted it alarm

linkage.renders: #link-verdict — whether pooling the issuer and origin ledgers yields an equality-testable match

mutations.kills: e2e/claims.spec.ts:36 expect(getByText('COLLUSION CHECK · LINKED: BLINDING WAS REMOVED')).toBeVisible()
mutations.observed: 1 failed / 12 passed: with blinding removed the page still claimed 'NO COMPUTABLE MATCH'

link-map.renders: #link-map — the drawn lines, one per computable link across the two ledgers

mutations.mutation: ignore the computed count and always emit a single line (`length: 1`)
mutations.observed: 1 failed / 12 passed: the partition fixture drew one line for two partitioned buckets

status.renders: #status — the live-region summary, whose good/alarm colour tracks whether protocol integrity held

mutations.mutation: ignore the integrity flag and always write `status good`
mutations.observed: 1 failed / 12 passed: the unblinded link alarm was reported in the pass colour

negative-claim.renders: #negative-claim — the §4.1d limitation, shown in the alarm palette only in the fixture that violates it

mutations.mutation: drop the `$('#negative-claim').removeAttribute('hidden')` call so the fixture renders without its limitation
